summary: Workers only inherit secrets registered before they fork, so to mask across all hosts in a task register on the controller beforehand. Masking matches exact strings (avoid short values), alternate encodings must be registered separately, but JSON-escaped forms are handled automatically.
questions: Why is a secret masked for one host but not others in the same task?
Are base64-encoded copies of a secret masked?
Should I register very short secrets?
Does masking catch JSON-escaped versions of a secret?

answer_card.title: Secret masking timing and matching
answer_card.answer_md:
- Already-running workers don't see secrets registered by other workers mid-task. Register on the controller first (vars plugin or `register_secret` filter in an earlier task) to mask across all hosts.
- Matching is exact substring, so avoid short/common values.
- Base64 or URL-encoded copies aren't masked; register those forms too.
- JSON-escaped forms (with or without `\uXXXX`) **are** derived and masked automatically.
